# Prefix owner identity and multi-client retention

V134 preserves the unfixed behavior: nine of 38 logical client-capacity assertions fail, and eight of 59 actual-model ownership/lineage assertions fail. Four distinct conversations retain only two ordinary entries; sequential followups hit only the last of four, versus all four for baseline. An unused snapshot can evict unrelated conversations on count or token pressure. Same IDs/images across loaded models incorrectly replace one another, or a foreign reusable entry suppresses storage of the current owner. These are cache behavior failures, not a new measured inference speed claim.

V135 includes model-bound duplicate matching, exact stored token-count validation, full-key ownership validation, atomic refusal when a new optional snapshot cannot fit without removing useful unrelated state, and first eviction of checkpoints that have neither supplied a hit nor returned as an ordinary conversation. A hit or ordinary return gives a checkpoint normal LRU standing. V135 passes 38 capacity, 63 owner/lineage, 172 ordinary retention, 180 MTP retention, 272 ordinary complete-prompt, 280 MTP complete-prompt and 209 combined image/MTP assertions: 1,214 total. Its standard catalogue fails only the old runtime fixtures that declare tokenCount zero while storing nonempty IDs (nine failed assertions in one group); all other groups pass.

V136 corrects those 13 logical fixture declarations, preserves normal priority when an ordinary entry is promoted into a reusable snapshot, adds the inverse-order regression, and registers client capacity in the standard catalogue. All 43 T0/T1 groups pass, plus 41 capacity, 63 owner/lineage, 272 ordinary full-prompt and 280 MTP full-prompt assertions (656 targeted assertions). Token and physical-state limits remain unchanged. Four ordinary clients retain their baseline followup hits; a fifth auxiliary request preserves the same three LRU survivors. Reused common prefixes, cancellation, image identity, sampled output and error recovery retain their tested behavior.

V136 frozen executable SHA-256: 0b1f2b33e97c7a35f6aafde565750085888d97d7419058d97601e22955e3193e; source archive bb77ba2b2dac2e7762ce98c07eeaf5db2697be6b24ad53b6497f7a6a26949df9; checks 860f80ceb1c524b6a9bef8b160b7f5c4c4bbf985a807a514835997f6782d909b. These diagnostic durations are correctness evidence only. Prior V133 repeat-prompt performance remains scoped to its frozen V114 executable; unique-request and final combined acceptance remain pending.
